the origin of life is a physicochemical process driven by cycling gradients of temperature, water and electromagnetic radiation, which leads to the emergence of living states through the coevolution of macromolecular surfaces and the evolution of molecular recognition.

life’s emergence follows from a high degree of physicochemical complexity and a high degree of crowdedness, and that non-covalent forces that determine molecular organization and cellular organization.

life’s emergence follows from a chemical and Darwinian coevolution, a high degree molecular complexity and a crowdedness, and the action of non-covalent intermolecular forces that determine molecular interactions and cellular organization.

the origin of life, the origin of heredity and the origin of Darwinian evolution.
the physicochemical principles that constrain current hypotheses about life’s origins to the natural processes of Darwinian evolution and the cycling of solar energy.
the emergence of life from chemical and Darwinial evolution under the constraints of molecular complexity and crowdedness and non-covalently driven molecular recognition.

life is the product of the interplay of the four above mentioned principles.

life’s origins follow from chemical and Darwinial evolution, a high molecular complexity, and a high degree of crowding, and non-co valent molecular forces that govern molecular recognition and cellular organisation.
life’s emergence follows from a physicochemical mechanism of molecular evolution that is based on the cycling gradients of solar radiation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the origin of life was not the result of an accident but of an evolutionarily driven, physicochemically controlled and Darwinian process.

the origin of life is the origin of a new physicochemical state of matter, the living state, which is characterized by the coevolution of macromolecules toward Darwinian thresholds of molecular information processing and cellular organization, and by the coevolving physicochemical organization of the cell interior toward a crowded, polarized and compartmentalized state of matter.
life’s emergence follows from physicochemical evolution, a high crowdedness and non-covalentic molecular forces that determine the molecular recognition and cellular organisation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
life’s emergence is not a chemical evolution that leads to the origin of the genetic code and the first cells.
the origin of life can be understood as a cyclic physiochemical process that makes Darwinian evolution observable in the context of living cells.
life is an emergent property of a crowded molecular system under cycling physicochemical gradients of temperature, water, ionic strength, electromagnetic radiation, and molecular crowding.
